flags.name: Flag 1 - CF Dashboard
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Navigate to the Insights and Logs tab from the left hand menu. From the dropdown select Dashboards.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
The Cloudflare dashboards provide a catalog of saved analytics views for reporting and investigation. Analytics Dashboards provide visualizations of your log data.

The Access event analytics dashboard lets users review login attempts to the applications they protected behind Access.

Set the event window to 30 days. Pay attention to Access events by type. What is the least common type?

</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="login">The flag is the type of access event.</s1-flag>

flags.name: Flag 2 - CF Dashboard
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Navigate to the Insights and Logs tab from the left hand menu. From the dropdown select Dashboards.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
The Cloudflare dashboards provide a catalog of saved analytics views for reporting and investigation. Analytics Dashboards provide visualizations of your log data.

The DNS query analytics dashboard lets users review queries handled by Gateway based on their DNS policies.

Set the event window to 30 days. Pay attention to the Gateway insights for DNS queries section.

</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="300">The flag is the number of DNS actions allowed by rule.</s1-flag>

hints.description: The flag is displayed under the DNS Action subsection.

flags.name: Flag 3 - CF Investigation
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Navigate to the soledrop.co domain. Find the Security page from the menu on the left. Select Web Assets from the dropdown. From the nav bar go to Upgrade.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
The API Shield preview tells users what endpoints need protecting, and can offer valuable analytics to help with incident prevention.

What is the endpoint destination for the top 5 discovered endpoints?
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="/api/...">The flag is the endpoint destination.</s1-flag>

hints.description: The flag is in the Endpoint column of the specified section.

flags.name: Flag 4 - CF Investigation
flags.token: Likely account takeover attacks detected in login requests
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Navigate to the soledrop.co domain. Find the Security page from the menu on the left. 
  
Select Analytics from the dropdown.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Under the Suspicious Acitvity section, what is the activity that has the highest number of related requests.
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="Traffic scored as attacks are reaching your origin">The flag is the name of the activity.</s1-flag>

hints.description: The flag is <s1-answer>Likely account takeover attacks detected in login requests</s1-answer>.

flags.name: Flag 5 - Oneflare Custom Dashboad
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Navigate to Dashboards on the SentinelOne console. Select Custom dashboards, then the Cloudflare dashboard. Set lookback window to 72 hours.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Custom dashboards are helpful because they allow analysts to display the information they think is most relevant. Dashboards allow this information to be readily accessible for threat analysis.

According to the custom Cloudflare dashboard, how many WAF (Web Application Firewall) blocks have occurred
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="100">The flag is the number of WAF blocks that have occurred.</s1-flag>

flags.name: Flag 6 - CF WAF Rule
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Navigate back to Security rules for the soledrop.co domain. </s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Now let's take a look at what is causing all those blocks.

In Cloudflare, how many WAF rules are in place AND active?
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="">The flag is the number of active WAF rules</s1-flag>

hints.description: While looking at custom security rules, count how many are involving WAF.

flags.name: Flag 7 - Oneflare Custom Dashboard
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Navigate to Dashboards on the SentinelOne console. Select Custom dashboards, then the Cloudflare dashboard. Set lookback window to 72 hours.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
According to the custom Oneflare dashboard, how many HTTP requests have we recieved within the last 72 hours
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="4000">The flag is the number of HTTPS requests recieved within the last 72 hours.</s1-flag>

flags.name: Flag 8 - HTTP Traffic
flags.description:
<s1-nav>On the left hand side navigate to Analytics. Select HTTP Traffic from the dropdown. Set the event window to 30 days.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
In HTTP Traffic, how many HTTP requests are going through CF?</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="100,000">The flag is the total number of HTTP requests</s1-flag>

flags.name: Flag 9 - DNS Tunneling
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Find the Alerts view from the menu on the left.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
From the Alerts view, locate the Alert cluster that has CF-Gateway-DNSTunnel — DNS Tunneling / C2 Beaconing (Gateway DNS) in the Alert name column.
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="30">The flag is the number of alerts in this cluster.</s1-flag>

flags.name: Flag 10 - DNS Tunneling
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Find the Alerts view from the menu on the left. 
From the Alerts view, locate the Alert cluster that has CF-Gateway-DNSTunnel — DNS Tunneling / C2 Beaconing (Gateway DNS) in the Alert name column. Click on any one of these alerts</s1-nav>

<s1-flag-body>
The Purple AI Alert description will be in the popup on the right hand side.
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="">The flag is what Purple AI says repeated long TXT queries are indicative of.</s1-flag>

flags.name: Flag 11 - DNS Tunneling
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Find the Alerts view from the menu on the left. 
From the Alerts view, locate the Alert cluster that has CF-Gateway-DNSTunnel — DNS Tunneling / C2 Beaconing (Gateway DNS) in the Alert name column. Click on any one of these alerts.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Use the Purple AI Alert Description to find the MITRE ATT&CK reference associated with Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol.
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="T####">The flag is the MITRE ATT&CK ID</s1-flag>

hints.description:
Read through the Purple AI Alert Description.

Find the MITRE ATT&CK ID that comes right before (Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol).

The code follows the following format: T####.

flags.name: Flag 12 - Mitigate
flags.description:
<s1-nav>Find the Alerts view from the menu on the left. 
From the Alerts view, locate the Alert cluster that has CF-Gateway-DNSTunnel — DNS Tunneling / C2 Beaconing (Gateway DNS) in the Alert name column. Click on any one of these alerts.</s1-nav>
<s1-flag-body>
Find the Actions button towards the top right of the alert. Click on the Actions button and proceed to mark the alert as a threat.
</s1-flag-body>
<s1-flag example="">The flag is the pair of threat policy options we have available to us.</s1-flag>
